facts.fact_text: At the material time the applicant was a district councillor.
The assembly was scheduled to take place from 6.30 to 8.30 p.m. on Thursday, 4 September 2003.
On 4 September 2003 a few dozen residents gathered on the Zashchitnikov Neba Square.
The applicant was among the residents who gathered on the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003.
At Krylatskoye district police station the applicant was placed in a cell.
On 3 September 2003 the prefect of the Western Administrative District of Moscow cancelled his previous decision of 29 August 2003 accepting the notice of the planned assembly.
The police dispersed the crowd at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003 by force.
At a nearby crossing, the police blocked the applicant's car.
The police held the driver of the applicant's car at gun-point.
The police took the applicant out of the car by force.
At Krylatskoye district police station the applicant was placed in a cell.
Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 was in force at the material time pursuant to Russian Presidential Decree no. 524 of 25 May 1992.

Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, organisers of an assembly were required to serve written notice on the municipal authorities no later than ten days before the planned assembly (§ 2).
Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, the municipal authority was required to give its response no later than five days before the assembly (§ 3).

Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, an assembly could be banned if its purpose was contrary to the Constitution or threatened public order or the security of citizens.

The provisional regulations on the procedure for notification of the executive branch of the Moscow authorities about meetings, street marches, demonstrations and pickets in streets, squares and other public places were approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993.

Under the provisional regulations approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993, notice of an assembly was to be served by the assembly organisers on the executive body between the fifteenth and tenth day before the planned assembly (§ 2).

Under the provisional regulations approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993, the executive body could refuse to accept the notice if the purpose of the assembly was contrary to the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, generally accepted public morals, if there was no undertaking on the part of the organisers to ensure public safety, if the assembly coincided in time and place with another one, if it threatened normal functioning of companies or organisations, or if it required suspending public or rail transport (§ 4).

Under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, disobedience of a lawful order or demand of a police officer is punishable by an administrative fine or by up to fifteen days' administrative detention (administrativnyi arest).

Under Article 27.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, administrative arrest — a temporary restriction of liberty of an individual — may be ordered in exceptional circumstances where it is necessary for a correct and prompt examination of the administrative case.

The prefect cancelled his decision of 29 August 2003 "in connection with the operative information of law-enforcement authorities about an expected outbreak of terrorist activities in the Krylatskoye district and with a view to ensuring the safety of the district's residents".

In the letter of 2 September 2003, the head of the police command of the Western Administrative District asked the prefect to annul his decision of 29 August 2003 because the police command "had received, from various sources, information about potential terrorist attacks in Moscow, in places of mass gatherings".

The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that the prefect's decision of 3 September 2003 was issued not in connection with the notice filed by the assembly organisers but in connection with a threat of increasing terrorist activities in the areas of mass gatherings, with a view to ensuring the security of the Krylatskoye District's residents.

The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that the actions of the Krylatskoye district police, which were aimed at preventing the mass action from taking place in connection with a real threat to life, health and security of citizens, were compatible with the Moscow regulations on co-ordinated police action during mass assemblies and the requirements of Article 17 § 3 of the Russian Constitution.

The prefect cancelled his decision of 29 August 2003 "in connection with the operative information of law-enforcement authorities about an expected outbreak of terrorist activities in the Krylatskoye district and with a view to ensuring the safety of the district's residents".
On 16 December 2003 Krylatskoye police station replied that there had been no operative information in their possession.

On 21 January 2004 the police command of the Western Administrative District of Moscow replied that the material requested was classified as secret and for that reason could not be made available to the judge.

In the letter of 2 September 2003, the head of the police command of the Western Administrative District asked the prefect to annul his decision of 29 August 2003 because the police command "had received, from various sources, information about potential terrorist attacks in Moscow, in places of mass gatherings".

The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that the prefect's decision of 3 September 2003 was issued not in connection with the notice filed by the assembly organisers but in connection with a threat of increasing terrorist activities in the areas of mass gatherings, with a view to ensuring the security of the Krylatskoye District's residents.

The applicant submitted on appeal that not a single public gathering organised by the Moscow mayor's office in the framework of the "Day of the City" had been cancelled as a result of a potential terrorist threat.
On 8 April 2004 the Moscow City Court, in summary fashion, rejected the applicant's appeal against the Kuntsevskiy District Court's judgment of 30 January 2004.
The applicant was not given any food or drink while detained at Krylatskoye district police station.
The judge of the Kuntsevskiy District Court ordered the applicant's release at 5.10 p.m. on 5 September 2003.

The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that the applicant's arrest had been lawful because the Russian Constitution only required a judicial decision if the relevant period of custody exceeded forty-eight hours.

The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that the administrative case against the applicant had been discontinued on a formal ground — the expiry of the prescription period — rather than by a finding of his innocence.

The Kuntsevskiy District Court dismissed the applicant's civil claim on the ground that Article 1070 of the Civil Code did not provide for State officials' liability for non-pecuniary damage incurred through unlawful administrative arrest.
On 14 April 2005 the Presidium of the Moscow City Court quashed the Kuntsevskiy District Court's decision of 6 July 2004 dismissing the applicant's civil claim.
On 14 April 2005 the Presidium of the Moscow City Court remitted the applicant's civil claim for a fresh examination.
On 16 November 2005 the Kuntsevskiy District Court dismissed the applicant's civil claim for damages again.
The Kuntsevskiy District Court noted that in cases of administrative arrest, State officials would be liable for non-pecuniary damage only if a fault on their part were proven.
The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that State officials had acted within their competence and powers and therefore could not be held liable for non-pecuniary damage sustained by the applicant.
On 2 March 2006 the Moscow City Court, on an appeal by the applicant, upheld the judgment of 16 November 2005 of the Kuntsevskiy District Court.
The Moscow City Court endorsed, in summary fashion, the Kuntsevskiy District Court's reasoning in its judgment of 16 November 2005.
